presentation.summary: Reports on what your users watch: activity over time, per-user sessions and stream types, and a breakdown of movies, shows and audiobooks by plays, time or smart plays.
presentation.description_markdown:
Playback Reporting adds a **Playback Reporting** page to the admin menu. It reads Silo's own playback history, so it needs no database of its own and shows plays recorded before it was installed.

- **Activity**: a bar graph of watch time, plays or smart plays per day, week or month, stacked by user (or by profile), media type or stream type, with a weekday-and-hour heatmap.
- **Users**: pick a user or profile to see their total watch time, movies, episodes and audiobooks, how they stream (Direct Play, Remux, Transcode), and every playback session.
- **Breakdown**: top movies, TV shows and audiobooks by plays, time, or smart plays, as a ranked list or a pie chart.
- **History**: every play in a date range, with CSV export.

**Smart plays** divide watch time by the length of the movie, episode or book, so two half-watched episodes count as one episode watched.

Watch time is the time actually watched (Silo's measured watch time). Plays recorded before Silo measured watch time use an estimate and are marked with ≈.

Settings let you hide plays shorter than a number of seconds and ignore accounts or profiles. Chart colors are picked on the report page under **Customize**. These only change the reports; Silo's history is untouched.

Audiobooks appear when they are played in Silo's own apps. Listening in Audiobookshelf apps is not part of Silo's playback history.

Optionally, the plugin can also record each play's client and whether it was local or remote, by watching live sessions. That setting is off by default.
presentation.setup_markdown:
1. In **Settings → API keys**, create a key on an **admin** account with no scopes. The plugin reads admin playback history, which no narrower scope covers yet, so the key can do anything that admin can. Keep it private.
2. Open this plugin's settings, paste the key under **Silo connection**, and save.
3. Open **Playback Reporting** from the admin menu. The first load can take a few seconds on a large history.
4. Optional: turn on **Track clients** to also report which apps and networks plays came from. It only covers plays that start after you turn it on.

capabilities.description: Serves the Playback Reporting admin page and its data.

global_config_schema.title: Silo connection
global_config_schema.description: How the plugin reads this server's playback history. Create the key under Settings → API keys, on an admin account, with no scopes.

fields.label: Admin API key
fields.description: Starts with sa_. Stored encrypted by Silo and only sent to this server.

fields.label: Server address (optional)
fields.description: Leave empty to reach Silo directly inside its own process. Set it only if the plugin runs somewhere that cannot, for example http://silo:8080.

global_config_schema.title: Report filters
global_config_schema.description: Plays the reports leave out. Silo's own history is not changed.

fields.label: Hide plays shorter than (seconds)
fields.description: Leave out plays watched for less than this, such as a few seconds of a trailer or an accidental start. 0 shows every play.

fields.label: Ignore list
fields.description: One per line. A username leaves out all of that account's plays; username/profile leaves out one profile, for example kids/Guest.

global_config_schema.title: Optional reports
global_config_schema.description: Extra data the plugin can collect beyond Silo's playback history.

fields.label: Track clients
fields.description: Watch live sessions every 15 seconds and remember each play's client app and whether it was local or remote. Covers plays that start after it is turned on; very short plays can be missed.
